newsitem.title: USA: CBOE fined over documents in wrongful death suit.
newsitem.headline: CBOE fined over documents in wrongful death suit.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange was fined by a Chicago circuit court judge for failing to produce documents in a wrongful death suit brought against the exchange, according to court documents dated March 12.
The CBOE was fined $500 and ordered to pay all court reporter costs and attorneys' fees, according to the order by Cook County Circuit Judge Kathy Flanagan.
CBOE officials were not available for comment Thursday.

The CBOE was charged with withholding documents relating to the collapse of trader Ronald Rzepiela on the CBOE trading floor on November 29, 1994. Rzepiela was taken to a hospital emergency room where he died.
The suit focuses on an alleged delay of about eight minutes following Rzepiela's collapse before action was taken.

John Kelly, the attorney representing Rzepiela's wife Patricia, said the existence of new documents relating to Rzepiela's case emerged at a recent deposition of Thomas Koppitz, who oversees operations at the CBOE.
The original suit was filed in February 1995.
The CBOE and co-defendants the Chicago Options Exchange Building Corp, Stanley Smith Security and Medteam Inc still face a wrongful death suit from Patricia Rzepiela.
